title: fetch, ReadableStream, and Web Streams API
hook: fetch returns a Response whose body is a ReadableStream — you can pipe megabytes from Redis-backed API to disk without buffering the entire payload in memory, using the same Web Streams API in browsers and Node 18+.

blocks.text: **fetch(url, init)**: Promise<Response> with headers, status, **body** stream. **ReadableStream**: source of chunks; **WritableStream**: sink; **TransformStream**: map chunks. **Backpressure**: slow consumer pauses producer. **pipeTo/pipeThrough** chain streams. Node `stream/promises.pipeline` integrates Node streams with Web streams.

entries.plainDefinition: Standard API for streaming byte/source data.
Producer slows when consumer buffer full.

blocks.text: Loading 500MB export via `await res.text()` OOMs Node — stream to file. SSE and chat apps read body reader in loop. Redis cached responses still benefit from streaming parse.

blocks.title: body consumed once
blocks.body: Response body stream can only be read once — clone() before two consumers.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Buffers 1GB response in memory. Cannot explain ReadableStream. No abort on long fetch.

interviewTakeaways: reader.read() loop or pipeTo for processing.
60s: fetch returns stream body. pipe to file without full buffer. AbortSignal cancels. clone for two reads. Node Readable.fromWeb bridges APIs.
